title: Agentic Engineering Through Models
claim: *Agentic engineering through models.* Modeling, realization, and evaluation recur as a system evolves. Alignment operates throughout; governance conversion can make a consequential lesson durable during any activity.
purpose: Show that governance conversion spans all recurring agentic engineering activities rather than adding another phase.
alt: Model, Realize, and Evaluate form a repeating cycle. A brace spans all three activities and is labeled Governance conversion: Make consequential lessons durable. Conversion can occur during any activity; it is not a fourth phase.
bw_encoding: White process boxes, black labels, black flow arrows and brace; no tonal role needed.
typography: Bundled Source Sans 3; 11.5pt bold title, 11pt regular activities, 11pt bold governance label, 10.5pt regular explanation.
routing: Orthogonal cycle edges; 45bp horizontal arrows and 20bp return approach. Native TikZ brace spans all three activities.
redesign: Separate recurring engineering activities from governance conversion, which can occur during any of them. A return arrow indicates repetition, and a brace spans every activity. Alignment remains throughout the work rather than a new phase.

validation.validation_scope: New cycle artwork only; final assembled chapter requires layout inspection.
